steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Uncle Saen, Aunt Isha, where... where are you going?

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: We've driven those bad guys from the Fraser Institute away! Let's have a celebration feast tonight. I'll invite Hella and the others...

steps.speaker: Female Refugee
steps.content: Thani, you've already done more than enough.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: What... what do you mean?
The woman standing before her didn't answer, simply placing a warm hand on top of her head.
In the distance, the sun was slowly being swallowed.

steps.speaker: Female Refugee
steps.content: We adults have only survived this long because of your care, even though you're still just a child yourself...
Those hands gently pressed down, and just as they were about to withdraw, Thani grabbed them tightly.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Please don't say that...

steps.speaker: Male Refugee
steps.content: We can't go on like this anymore. We need to take responsibility and protect our children... Thani, take the kids and go.

steps.speaker: Female Refugee
steps.content: Remember, we aren't abandoning you. Someday, you'll understand...
[Exit Flashback]

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: But I never did understand...

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: I don't understand why the adults did what they did.
Thani cradles the smaller girl in her arms as blood gradually soaks through their clothes, rivulets of it trickling down their bodies. Sobs slowly well up from her throat.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Why... Why would they choose to separate from their families, to be transformed forever into... that... just to gain some so-called power...

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Every day, I dream about all of us being together again. Even in the harshest desert, even with countless enemies hunting us, I wouldn't be afraid... We could have rebuilt a home together and lived our lives properly.
She takes a deep breath and looks up at you.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Chief... it never could have been possible, could it? In a world like this... how could we ever live the kind of life I imagine?

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: It's like... it's like the fruit trees outside the refugee camp. We picked them too often until they couldn't bear fruit anymore... Just like how I was abandoned by my parents to begin with, left alone without any family.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: I know it. I've always known it. I'm not a child anymore. I can't keep running away like this forever.
Thani raises her hand and clutches your sleeve tightly, leaving dark, damp marks on the fabric.
She yanks you forward suddenly, pulling you into her intense gaze.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: I can't stand by and watch my family die again. I want to protect everyone with my own hands...
Tears stream continuously from her eyes, but not for a moment does she close them.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Chief, I want the shackles!

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: I want to protect everyone, even if it means I cannot be with them...

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Even so, I still want to protect them!
Release the shackles
In an instant, countless unfamiliar memories flood into your mind.
A pair of hands brushes away the sand and gently cradles you, a swaddled infant.
This baby has red eyes... how strange. Look, she's even smiling.
How extraordinary. She's bound to have a bright future. Let's give her a name. What about... Thani?
Someone fills the bowl in your hands with soup, a few wild berries floating on its surface. Warmth radiates from the bottom of the bowl into your palms.
Eat up, though it's not much of a meal...
Thani, if it weren't for the medicine you brought, Shura and I would've...
Heh, she even said she wanted to follow your example to improve our living conditions. As her mom, I should have been the one giving her a better life...
The girl standing before you opens her palm, revealing a tiny, shriveled fruit.
Thani! You don't know me, but my mom says you're our hero! Hehe, in my heart, you're even cooler than Synex!
I just found this outside. It's sweet and delicious! It's for you! If I can find more tomorrow, I'll bring you another one!
Oh right, my name...
It's Shura!
The next moment, a strange sensation pulls you back to reality. A gust of wind seems to brush against your skin, yet you haven't moved.
You look up to see Thani darting past, sliding between you and the assassin. She circles around the attacker in one fluid motion before extending her foot to land a precise kick.
The other assassin has already lunged forward, sword drawn, but Thani moves faster than the blade itself. She strikes the assassin's wrist with a powerful blow.
The dagger tumbles to the ground as the assassin angrily swipes back to grab her, but Thani has already nimbly sprung backward, evading his reach.
Having done all that, Thani rushes back to your side, the air stirring around her from her speed.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: They move fast, but... I can see them clearly.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: ...The one on the left will come at us in three seconds!
Just as Thani finishes speaking, the assassin on the left leaps up, but she simply sidesteps the blow with grace. The blade slices through empty air and crashes against the rock.
You seize an opening and drive your foot into his knee. He grunts in pain and staggers backward. Pressing forward, you follow with a crushing elbow strike to his throat.
Meanwhile, Thani seizes the moment to scoop up a handful of gravel from the ground and fling it at the other assassin's eyes.

The two assassins stumble back a few steps. At that moment, the roar of engines erupts from behind distant sand dunes. You look up to see a helicopter rapidly closing in, its cabin door wide open and gun barrels aimed at the ground below.

steps.speaker: Task Force Operative
steps.content: Get down!
You grab Thani and pull her to the ground. A split second later, gunfire erupts as precise bullet shots strike the ground around the assassins' feet, forcing them into complete submission.

Amid the thundering gunfire, you feel Thani wrench herself free from your grasp. You instinctively reach for her, but your fingers only brush the fluttering hem of her clothes as she scrambles desperately toward the other girl.

steps.speaker: Shura
steps.content: Thani...? Is that... you?
As the two assassins are pinned to the ground, the gunfire gradually ceases.
You hear leather boots approaching from behind. A sound that normally would bring you complete relief.

steps.speaker: Task Force Operative
steps.content: Chief, we've neutralized all enemies in the area!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Someone has been wounded here.

Before you all, the two girls huddle together, their faces softly illuminated by moonlight. You don't really need to look for Thani's hands. They're pressed against Shura's abdomen, desperately trying to stop the blood gushing out between her fingers.
Despite the thundering helicopter rotors, you can hear the girls' voices clearly.

steps.speaker: Shura
steps.content: Thani... am I... am I finally as strong... as you?...

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Of course... you're our brave little Shura.

steps.speaker: Shura
steps.content: Will you... will you miss me?
Thani reaches out to wipe the girl's face clean, but tears keep falling, mixing with the sand and dust and sticking stubbornly to her skin.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Do you remember the story I told you?

steps.speaker: Shura
steps.content: Thani... that story you told me... it's true, isn't it?

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Yes, yes.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: We will never be apart. Never ever.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: You'll stay with me, and I'll always stay with you. Forever and ever.

steps.speaker: Shura
steps.content: Just like... how we've been... together on our journey...

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Yes, just like how we've been together on our journey.
Reassured by the answer, the girl closes her eyes with a smile on her face.
She's about to have a very long dream.
In her dream, moonlight pours down over the warmly lit homes, while the white sand beneath her feet sparkles like the milky way.
[Scene Change]
The mission is over. You will bring Thani and the children back to DisCity. Afterward, these kids from the refugee camp will be placed in an orphanage in the city to begin their new lives.
Thani will follow you back to the Bureau to receive medical treatment.
This time, she doesn't refuse.
Before your official departure, you and Thani come to the desert to say goodbye to your friend.
Along the way, Thani cradles a small box in her arms with great care, walking in silence.
Suddenly, she snaps out of her daze, looks at you, and breaks into a smile.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Chief, do you remember that song I sang before?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Of course I remember.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Actually, an elderly lady from the refugee camp taught me that song. She also told me a story.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Legend says that everyone born in WhiteSands is blessed by the Desert Goddess. When our bodies perish, our souls will transform into a single grain of sand in WhiteSands, living on in this world forever.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Which means that, here in the desert, if you close your eyes and listen with your heart, you can hear the voices of your departed loved ones in the wind.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: I've shared this story before, but no one really seemed to believe it. Chief, do you believe it?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Yes, I believe all of you have been blessed.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm sorry... but it's a beautiful story.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Hehe, actually, I didn't believe it before! Like I said, I wasn't a little kid anymore!

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Granny got a bit forgetful in her later years. She would often mix up elements of the story. Sometimes it was the Desert Goddess's blessing, other times it was the Wind God's. Eventually, I had to remind her of her original version.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: If that story was really true, why couldn't she remember it properly?

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Besides, after I got sick, I spent so much time listening to the wind. But even with my super-hearing, I never once caught Granny's song.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Thani...

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: But now I believe it. Because last night, I saw your memories.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Why do you look so surprised? You obviously saw mine too!

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: I saw you fighting side by side with so many people, and they were all so amazing!

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Even though they looked a bit odd, just like the folks at the refugee camp, I could feel they were all good people!

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: They're your family, aren't they?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Yes. Every single one of them. My important family.
You raise your hand to your chest. The shackles vibrate slightly, as if responding to your words.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: So that's why we won! It was because they were helping us, wasn't it?

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Before yesterday, I wouldn't have even dared to imagine fighting those killers! But last night, it wasn't just the two of us in that battle. There were so many others cheering us on.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: So I think maybe Granny's story was true after all.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Our family will always watch over us. Even when they can't physically be by our side, even when... we can never see them again, their strength remains with us.
Thani bows her head, smiling down at the box in her hands.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: As long as the wind keeps blowing, we'll always be together. After all, don't we all share the same sky above us?
She opens the box, and the wood makes a soft sound, like a child's mischievous giggle.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: So I believe she'll always be with me.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Shura.
Her voice catches, tears threatening to fall at any moment and dampen the ashes in the container.
But you see no tears. When she lifts her face to the wind again, there's only a radiant smile.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Bless me, Shura.
She raises her hands, holding the box up to the wind.
You watch as the white sand before you gets scattered by the wind, then gathers together again before drifting away into the distance.
The wind continues to blow. On this stretch of the mortal world, you seem to hear the whispered murmurs of countless old friends, carried by the breeze coming from behind, gently embracing you.
Beside you, Thani begins humming that song again. Her voice catches before she finishes the first bit of the melody, but she quickly resumes softly, never faltering again.
...In my dreams I light my lanterns, gazing up at the stars from the ruins.
My friend who saw me off, are you singing the same song too?
[Scene Change]
It's another ordinary day at the Bureau. You've just finished a meeting and are heading back to your office.
[Blank Screen] Effect
You sense someone's presence.
Thani is clinging to the wall with her four limbs, an overstuffed backpack strapped to her back.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Thani, what are you up to again?

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Shh... I'm going to visit Kash and the others at the orphanage.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You don't need to sneak around like this to leave the Bureau. Just file a request.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: No way! This is part of my training. If I can avoid triggering the alarms this time, it means I've gotten stronger!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Okay. Just be careful...
Before you can finish your sentence, you hear a loud crash. Almost simultaneously, pain shoots through your body as a massive weight slams into you.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Waaah! Why is the floor so slippery today?!
The contents of her bag scatter across the floor. A can rolls right to your feet.
Thani lies flat on her back, having managed to save only a bag of fruit. She can't help but laugh at herself as she clutches the heavy bag to her chest.
From the other end of the corridor, a mechanical female voice speaks.

steps.speaker: Labyrinth
steps.content: Labyrinth is here to report that today's floor waxing has been completed. Master may inspect the results whenever you want.
